reproduced:
I could not refute the bit-exactness. I checked the commits from git archive (base ef5caee8, new 9b73dd78), not the working trees.
1. Bench ARM=1: all 22 hashes are the same. The instruction counts match the report (volume 3918 → 945, phaser 19947 → 11582, chorus 8928 → 5751, EQ 7210 → 4021, bitcrush 723 → 445).
2. Own extreme cases (scratchpad/adv/adv.cpp) ran on ARM, with the same hashes in both trees. Covered were all 5 mod FX types plus EQ, block sizes 1–9, 15–17, 31–34, 63–65, 95–97, 100, 127 and 128, runs of 20–40 blocks, states and parameters at INT32_MIN/MAX, and full scale at Nyquist. For volume, send, pan, ramp, mono and addTo were added (also addTo == buffer), for the SRR positions at the limits 4194303/4194304/0xFFFFFFFF. A deliberately inserted mutation of the ramp changed the hash, so the test works.
3. Song trace with --init-sounds --seed 1: all 165,312 calls identical (cmp), measured.wav also identical. The demand drops from 1,095,569 to 1,035,133. The offsets in the tracer are plausible (LFO phase +128·rate, write index +128).
4. Code review: waveform, order, wrap and saturation are the same as before, all paths including Grain without a buffer are kept, and there is no overlap of buffers at the call sites. GCC derived the :64 hints via IPA. The addresses are right: soundBuffer 0x200828a0, renderingBuffer and reverbBuffer 32-aligned, globalEffectableBufferMemory alignas(32).
5. With -Wall -Wextra -O2 there are no new warnings (216 instead of 218). The stack grows by +120/+320/+24 B, the .bin by 2512 B, clang-format is clean, and the patch matches the commit.
